sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The Backlog module is the v5 demand-pipeline surface — it replaces v4's portfolio intake. It shows every project that hasn't yet entered active execution: anything from a fresh idea (DoI 0) to an approved-but-not-yet-started project (DoI 2). The module is reachable at `/backlog` and offers two complementary views: a **Cube view** (visual matrix of t-shirt size × Composite Score, helpful for portfolio-shape conversations) and a **List view** (sortable, filterable table — useful for ranking discussions and cutoff decisions). Use the cube during roadmap reviews; use the list when you need to defend a specific cutoff line.

sections.title: Tech Navigator scoring
sections.body:
Every transformation project carries a **scoring profile** with 6 sub-criteria split into two dimensions:
- **Complexity (3 sub-criteria)** — Standardization (40%), Usage (40%), Maintenance (20%). Each scored 1–5.
- **Value Creation (3 sub-criteria)** — Financial (50%), Payback (40%), Competitive (10%). Each scored 1–5.
- **2 reserved slots** — admin-configurable additional sub-criteria for future taxonomy evolution.
The rubric weights live in Admin → Planning Parameters under `param_group='tech_navigator'` and are admin-editable. The system computes a **Composite Score** (weighted average across both dimensions) and infers a **t-shirt size** (XS / S / M / L / XL) from the project's `total_budget` against admin-configurable thresholds.

Click any project row to open the detail panel — four tabs:
- **Scores tab** — interactive rubric with per-sub-criterion 1–5 selector. Score cells turn amber when the project is below cutoff.
- **Financial tab** — total budget, run rate, t-shirt size derivation.
- **Master Data tab** — project type (1/2/3), transformation level (T0/T1/T2), responsible PL, governance metadata.
- **Milestones tab** — baseline + forecast date ranges per milestone.

sections.title: Pipeline + DoI lifecycle
sections.body:
Projects in the backlog progress through stages governed by two parallel concepts:
- **Pipeline stage** (working name per `[A-PS-02]`) — narrative state used for storytelling: `idea`, `under_review`, `pitch_board`, `approved`, `in_execution`, `operate`. Stage names are admin-configurable.
- **DoI (Degree of Implementation)** 0–5 per `[A-DOI-01]` — concrete maturity score:
  - 0–4 = Change (the project is in flight or pre-flight).
  - 5 = Run (it has reached steady state and is now an Offering or Internal Service).

Advancement gates: DoI 2→3 requires an active BTC profile when `to_business_pct > 0`. DoI 4→5 requires the project to be 'go-live' complete. The Backlog only shows DoI 0–2 entries; once a project advances to DoI 3 it leaves the Backlog and appears in the Change Portfolio.

sections.title: Within-cutoff ranking
sections.body:
Projects are ranked by Composite Score using admin-editable ranking weights. The **cutoff line** is a budget threshold (sum of total budgets in rank order until the planning envelope is hit) — projects above the line get the `within_cutoff = true` flag, projects below get `within_cutoff = false`.

The Backlog header shows '11 above · 0 below'-style counts and a 'Filter to within-cutoff' toggle. The cube view shades below-cutoff cells differently. The cutoff is recomputed whenever a project is added, scored, or has its `total_budget` edited; the recomputation is server-side and idempotent.

sections.title: Send-back / resubmit cycle
sections.body:
When a Controller spots an issue with a backlog entry — an unrealistic budget, an incomplete Tech Navigator score, missing master data — they can **send it back** to the responsible PL with a justification. The project's pipeline stage moves to `sent_back` and it becomes editable by the PL. Send-back events are recorded in the Audit Log under category `pipeline_transitions`.

The PL fixes the issue and clicks **Resubmit**, which moves the project back to its prior stage. The cycle is fully audited end-to-end: every send-back / resubmit pair appears in the project's History tab with timestamps, actors, and the controller's justification text. Use this flow to demonstrate the controller-PL feedback loop without needing a CR.

sections.title: AI Council gate
sections.body:
Projects whose total budget exceeds the AI-Council threshold (admin-editable, defaults to a high six-figure value) require explicit AI Council approval before they can advance past DoI 2. Two columns surface this:
- **`ai_council_approved`** — boolean; defaults false; only Controllers can flip it.
- **`ai_council_doc_url`** — a URL pointing to the council's approval minutes.

A project flagged for AI Council review shows a small chip in the Backlog list and an info card in the detail panel; the advancement endpoint returns 403 if the gate isn't satisfied. Use this to demonstrate governance hooks for high-budget initiatives without leaving the demo data.

sections.title: Role-based access
sections.body:
- **Controller** — full access; can score / re-score, advance pipeline stages, send back, flip AI Council, edit cutoff weights.
- **Project Lead** — sees own projects; can resubmit a sent-back project; can edit its master data and Tech Navigator scores.
- **Cost Center Owner** — read-only on the Backlog (relevant when a backlog entry references resources from their CC).
- **Executive** — read-only; useful when running portfolio reviews — open the cube view, walk through cutoff line conversation.
